lesson.title: Quadratic–Linear Systems
intro: A quadratic–linear system contains one quadratic equation and one linear equation.
The solutions to the system are the points where the line and the parabola intersect.
A quadratic–linear system may have zero, one, or two solutions depending on how the graphs intersect.

workedExample.problem: Solve the system y = x² − 4 and y = x.
steps: Set the equations equal to each other: x² − 4 = x.
Solve the quadratic equation to find the x-values.
Substitute each x-value into y = x to find the ordered pairs.
workedExample.answer: The solutions are the intersection points of the line and parabola.

questions.prompt: Consider the system of equations y = x² − 4 and y = x. How many solutions does the system have?
questions.explanation: Set the equations equal: x² − 4 = x. Rearranging gives x² − x − 4 = 0, which has two real solutions. Therefore the line and parabola intersect at two points.

questions.prompt: Which equation results from substituting y = x into the quadratic equation y = x² − 4 to solve the system?
questions.explanation: Substitute y = x into y = x² − 4 to get x = x² − 4. Rearranging gives x² − x − 4 = 0.
